summary: Philip L. Quinn worked in philosophy and religious studies. He studied at Georgetown University (~1958–1962), the University of Delaware (~1962–1966), and the University of Pittsburgh (~1966–1970). He held posts at Brown University (~1971–1985) and the University of Notre Dame (~1985–2004).

Philip Whalen was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He studied at Reed College (~1946–1951) and under Richard Baker (~1972–1983). His posts included visiting poet at Naropa University, resident teacher at South Ridge Zendo, and abbot at Hartford Street Zen Center (~1991–2002).

Philipp A. Maas works in Indology and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Bonn (~1998–2004) under Claus Vogel and Albrecht Wezler. His posts include the University of Bonn, University of Vienna (~2004–2013), Austrian Academy of Sciences (~2006–2014), and Leipzig University (~2019).

Philippe Turenne specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and completed his PhD at McGill University (~2003–2010) supervised by Thupten Jinpa and G. Victor Sōgen Hori, also studying under Khenpo Palden Sherab.

Philippe-Édouard Foucaux worked in Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies, having studied under Eugène Burnouf (~1838–1852). He held posts at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales (~1842–1854), the Collège de France (1857–1894), and the University of Paris (~1862–1894).
Phillip B. Zarrilli worked in Indology and other fields. He held academic posts at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1979–1998) and the University of Exeter (~1999–2020).

Phillip E. Bloom specializes in Sinology, history/archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at Harvard University (~2006–2013) under doctoral supervisors Eugene Y. Wang, Yukio Lippit, and James Robson.

Phra Brahmagunabhorn works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned degrees from Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (~1958–1961) and Sukhothai Thammathirat Open University (~-1982), serving as Dean of the Faculty of Buddhist Studies and Deputy Vice Rector at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (~1964–1976).

Phra Brahmapundit works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He served as Rector at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (~1997–2018), Chairperson of the International Council for the Day of Vesak (~2004), and President of the International Association of Buddhist Universities (~2007).

Phra Kiattisak Ponampon works in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned an MA at the University of Otago (~2013–2015), supervised by Xiaohuan Zhao, Will Sweetman, and Elizabeth Guthrie, and also studied under Jinhua Chen, Stephen R. Bokenkamp, and others in 2013.

Phra Sigambhirayan specializes in Buddhist studies. He studied at Sukhothai Thammathirat Open University and Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University, later serving as Dean of the Graduate School at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University in 1998.

Phramaha Niras Ruangsan specializes in Buddhist studies. He earned his Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Sydney (~2009–2015) under the supervision of Edward Fitzpatrick Crangle, Peter Oldmeadow, Mark Allon, and Prayong Seanburan.
Phramaha Somboon Watana works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He completed a PhD at Panjab University (1999–2003) under the doctoral supervision of Rekha Jhanji and Dharmanand Sharma.

Phramonchai Saitanaporn works in Buddhist studies. He completed a Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Sydney (~2005–2009) under supervisor Edward Fitzpatrick Crangle, committee member Jeff Wilson, and traditional teacher Phrathepyanmahamuni.

Phuntshok Tashi works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1982–1987) and the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (~1987–1989), and held a post at the National Museum of Bhutan (~2005).

Phyllis Granoff specializes in Indology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Radcliffe College (~1965–1969) and Harvard University (~1969–1973), and held posts at McMaster University (~1976–2004), Yale University (~2004), and the University of Toronto Mississauga.
Pia Conti works in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. She studied under teachers Peter Sharrock and Tadeusz Skorupski.

Pierce Salguero works in Buddhist studies, history/archaeology, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Virginia (~2003–2005) and Johns Hopkins University (~2005–2010), holding posts at Pennsylvania State University (2010) and the University of Pennsylvania (2011–2012).

Pierre Amédée Jaubert was a scholar of linguistics and other fields who studied at the École nationale des langues orientales vivantes (~1795–1798). He later held posts there (~1820–1847), at the Société Asiatique (1834–1847), and at the Collège de France (1838–1847).
Pierre-Sylvain Filliozat worked in Indology and linguistics. He held posts at the Institut Français de Pondichéry (~1963–1967) and the École des hautes études en sciences sociales (~1967–2005).
